subject: Re: ML opt-out confirmation + subprocessor transfer matrix
messages:
From: Claire Jones <claire.jones@novamed.com>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novamed.com
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ML opt-out confirmation + subprocessor list request

Hi Stephanie / Karthik,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. As discussed in the demo, NovaMed needs written confirmation that any customer data we provide to Redwood will not be used to improve or retrain Redwood models (no-training / no-improvement commitment) and that prompt/response ownership remains with NovaMed.

To move this through procurement we need:
- Draft contract language we can insert into the DPA (short clause is fine)
- A current subprocessor map (who has access to customer request data) and an indication of any planned subprocessor transfers in the next 12 months
- A plain-English description of how we can export our data (SFTP/API) and a sample of operational evidence you can provide showing the no-train toggle and attestations
- Any cross-border transfer matrix (which data centers / regions could process data)

Can you share a draft by EOD Tuesday (PST)? Procurement is on a tight cadence.

Claire Jones
Sr. PM, AI Integrations
NovaMed

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Jones <claire.jones@novamed.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-16T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: ML opt-out confirmation + subprocessor list request

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide the materials you need. High level plan and deliverables:

1) Draft DPA appendix clause (short, binding sentence) — attached as DPA_appendix_draft.pdf. This explicitly states: "Provider will not use Customer Data to train or improve Provider models; Customer retains ownership of prompts and outputs; Provider will not assert derivative rights."

2) Subprocessor map — attached as subprocessor_map.csv. It lists current subprocessors, data residency by region, and a flag for whether they touch request/response payloads. If any subprocessor transfers are planned in the next 12 months we will include a notice timeline.

3) Export + evidence options — we support SFTP export and API exports. For attestation, we can produce:
   - A one-time signed attestation from security that the no-train toggle was set for your tenant (PDF)
   - Operational logs showing toggle state changes and the KV cache behavior (sample attached: proof_of_toggle_sample.txt)

4) Cross-border processing matrix — summarized in the subprocessor CSV and a short paragraph in the appendix noting that requests may be routed to onshore capacity by request.

Next steps: Karhtik/Neha — can you verify the onshore KMS and SFTP export SLA text below and confirm there are no planned subprocessor movements for NovaMed in the next 12 months? If so, Claire, we can finalize the appendix for signature.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Trust & Compliance (Customer Security)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: DPA_appendix_draft.pdf (pdf), subprocessor_map.csv (csv), proof_of_toggle_sample.txt (txt)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-16T13:50:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: confirm export mechanics and residency

Stephanie / Neha — quick tech check to confirm the customer-facing language matches platform behavior:

- No-training toggle: tenant-level boolean stored in the control plane; when true, model improvement pipelines exclude that tenant's request/response traces from any training datasets. We have audit logs and a daily job that snapshots toggle states. The sample proof_of_toggle_sample.txt shows timestamped entries.

- Onshore KMS: For customers requiring onshore keys, we bind to their KMS via per-tenant CMKs in the us-west-2 region. That prevents key export outside the region.

- Exports: SFTP (push) and API (pull) are both supported; SFTP supports AES-256 encrypt-at-rest on the target bucket and a configurable retention window. Export job runs can be scheduled weekly/daily.

- Subprocessor transfers: There are no planned transfers that would affect NovaMed right now. We do have a planned beta of a new logging provider next year — not currently targeted at production tenants. We should include a clause committing to 30-day notice for any subprocessor additions that would access request/response payloads.

Action items: Neha — please produce the attestation PDF and a sanitized log extract for NovaMed. Steph — add the 30-day notice language to the appendix and confirm the SFTP SLA wording.

-Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Jones <claire.jones@novamed.com>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Final: DPA appendix language + operational proofs for NovaMed

Hi Claire — following up with the finalized language and proofs per your ask. Below is the exact clause we propose for insertion into the DPA as an appendix (legal-friendly but concise):

"Provider shall not use, process, or incorporate Customer Data (including prompts and generated outputs) for the purpose of developing, improving, or training any machine learning models or related services ('Model Improvement'). Provider further acknowledges that Customer retains all ownership rights in Customer prompts and outputs and will not assert any derivative rights. Provider will not transfer Customer Data to subprocessors for Model Improvement without explicit written consent. Provider commits to provide Customer with operational evidence of the no-training setting upon request, including audit logs and a signed attestation. Provider will give Customer no less than 30 calendar days' notice before onboarding any new subprocessor that may access request/response payloads."

Attached: DPA_appendix_draft.pdf (final), subprocessor_map.csv (current snapshot), proof_of_toggle_sample.txt (redacted log extract), and a short export-run checklist.

Let us know if procurement needs any further edits — we can fast-track a countersign if the language is acceptable.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Privacy & Integrations
Redwood Inference
